thread:
maya: getting paged for high p99 and continuous-batcher crashes in us-east-2. stack shows CUDA OOM and batch sizes exploding. starting here so we have a single thread for mitigation.
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD12345 triggered: continuous-batcher: high-latency and container-restarts (sev2) — routed to oncall.
pagerduty-bot: Alert details: ~2000 requests/min, cpu 95%, gpu mem pressure > 98%, multiple restarts in last 3m.
jonathan: I see repeated log pattern: 'batcher: queue length 0 -> 65k -> deadlock'. suspect unbounded accumulation when downstream worker fails.
anika: attaching a tail of the container logs from the hottest pod (cb-54):
```
[2026-01-22T14:12:07Z] batcher INFO enqueue size=128
[2026-01-22T14:12:08Z] batcher INFO batch_started size=128
[2026-01-22T14:12:08Z] runtime ERROR cuda out of memory when allocating 2048MB for KV cache
[2026-01-22T14:12:08Z] runtime WARN kernel fallback to CPU path
[2026-01-22T14:12:09Z] batcher INFO enqueue size=1024
[2026-01-22T14:12:10Z] batcher INFO enqueue size=8192
[2026-01-22T14:12:11Z] batcher ERROR batch growth detected: growth_factor=64 queue_len=65280
[2026-01-22T14:12:12Z] batcher FATAL deadlock detected, shutting down batcher thread
[2026-01-22T14:12:12Z] containerd ERROR process exited with status 137
```
leon: that growth_factor log is from the continuous-batching loop. looks like a bug where a backpressure check aborts but the enqueue loop keeps multiplying batch windows.
carol: customer-facing impact: multiple tenants hitting embeddings endpoints saw 10-30s tails and some 503s. ops dashboard: 40% of requests retried.
maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching globally, 2) cap batch size env to 256, 3) restart affected replicas, 4) enable fallback model variant (cpu quant) for overloaded routes.
jonathan: I'm going to flip the feature flag to disable continuous batching:
```
# k8s patch to env
kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher CONT_BATCHING_ENABLED=false --namespace=prod-us-east-2
kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher CONT_BATCH_MAX_SIZE=256 --namespace=prod-us-east-2
```
anika: applied the env changes to prod-us-east-2. scaling rolling restart:
```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher -n prod-us-east-2
```
ops-bot: Rolling restart started: 6 pods -> 6 pods (strategy: RollingUpdate)
maya: started increasing replica count on the fallback workers to absorb traffic while GPU pods recover:
```
kubectl scale deploy/fallback-worker --replicas=4 -n prod-us-east-2
```
leon: I see pod cb-54 restarted and then cb-57 OOM killed again. however after setting CONT_BATCHING_ENABLED=false, the queue growth stopped in logs for the new pods.
carol: notified the account reps; PSR draft: some requests experienced high latency and transient 503s between 14:11-14:27 UTC. no data exfiltration.
jonathan: root cause hypothesis: when runtime hits CUDA OOM and falls back to CPU path, the continuous-batching controller misinterprets the slow path as successful consumption and increases windowing. that causes upstream producers to keep batching more, leading to exponential enqueue.
maya: can we get heap/profile of batcher process for cb-54 before it restarts? any core dumps?
anika: collected /var/log/containers/cb-54-core.log and uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-archives/PD12345/cb-54-core.log. also captured a brief strace of the worker.
leon: putting a short-term circuit breaker in the admission controller: if queue_len > 10000, reject new enqueues with 429 and opaque Retry-After header. I will patch the proxy:
```
# NGINX lua rule (pseudo)
if queue_len() > 10000 then
  return ngx.exit(429)
end
```
maya: good. that's live on prod-us-east-2-canary. rolling to prod after validation.
incident-bot: Incident PD12345 severity updated to S2 -> S1 if customer retries increase; currently S2.
carol: which customers hit it the worst? rep list: alpha-inc, beta-saas. alpha-inc reported multiple timeouts and logs.
jonathan: alpha-inc traffic pattern triggered big batches (long prompts + streaming), pushed the runtime into large KV cache allocations, which then triggered CUDA OOMs.
manual: handoff to next oncall at 14:30 UTC. maya and jonathan to create a short postmortem doc and open a JIRA for continuous-batching fix.
maya: handoff to anika at 14:30 UTC — anika you're on for the remainder, please continue tracking and own the postmortem.
anika: acknowledged. next steps: 1) keep CONT_BATCHING_ENABLED=false until prod roll with fix, 2) patch controller to cap growth_factor, 3) add unit/integration tests simulating runtime fallback to CPU path, 4) postmortem with timeline and customer impact.
carol: drafting status update to customers now — will send PSR and internal incident comms.
leon: quick note for follow-up: add metric batcher.growth_factor and alert when > 8 for 30s, and instrument per-route batch size distributions.
maya: thanks team. will mark this thread as incident timeline and include in the final postmortem. tagging #eng-runtime #sre for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
